{{short description|Extinct Australian Aboriginal language}} {{Use dmy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Use Australian English|date=September 2011}} {{Infobox language |name = Ngawun |states = [[Australia]] |region = [[Cape York Peninsula]], [[Queensland]] |ethnicity = [[Ngawun]], [[Wanamara]] |extinct = 24 August 1977, with the death of Cherry O'Keefe ({{lang|nxn|Tjapun}}) |familycolor = Australian |fam1 = [[Pama–Nyungan languages|Pama–Nyungan]] |fam2 = [[Mayabic languages|Mayabic]] |lc1= nxn |ld1=Ngawun |lc2=wnn |ld2=Wunumara |glotto=ngaw1240 |glottoname=Ngawun |aiatsis=G17 |aiatsisname=Ngawun |aiatsis2=G16.1 |aiatsisname2=Wunumura }} '''Ngawun''' is an [[language extinction|extinct]] [[Mayi languages|Mayi language]] once spoken on the [[Cape York Peninsula]] of [[Queensland]], [[Australia]], by the Wunumara and [[Ngawun people]]s. The last speaker of the language was [[Cherry O'Keefe]] (or {{lang|nxn|Tjapun}} in the language) who died of [[pneumonia]] on 24 August 1977.{{cite book | first = Gavan | last = Breen | year = 1981 | title = The Mayi languages of the Queensland Gulf Country | location = Canberra | publisher = AIAS | isbn = 0-85575-124-X | page = 13}} The [[etymology]] of the name ''Ngawun'' is unknown. ''Wanamarra'' (also known as ''Maykulan'' and ''Wunumura)'' was spoken in [[North West Queensland]]. The language region includes areas within the [[Shire of Mckinlay|Shire of McKinlay]], [[Shire of Cloncurry]] and [[Shire of Richmond]], including the [[Flinders River]] area, and the towns of [[Kynuna]] and [[Richmond, Queensland|Richmond]].{{Cite SLQ-CC-BY|url=https://maps.slq.qld.gov.au/iyil/view/139|title=Wanamarra|website=Queensland Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages map|access-date=5 February 2020}} == Phonology == === Consonants === {| class="IPA wikitable" style="text-align: center;" ! rowspan="2" | ! colspan="2" |[[Peripheral consonant|Peripheral]] ! colspan="2" |[[Laminal consonant|Laminal]] ! colspan="2" |[[Apical consonant|Apical]] |- ![[Labial consonant|Labial]] ![[Velar consonant|Velar]] ![[Dental consonant|Dental]] ![[Alveolo-palatal consonant|Alveolo-
palatal]] ![[Alveolar consonant|Alveolar]] ![[Retroflex consonant|Retroflex]] |- ![[Plosive consonant|Plosive]] |p |k |t̪ |t̠ʲ |t |ʈ |- ![[Nasal stop|Nasal]] |m |ŋ |n̪ |n̠ʲ |n |ɳ |- ![[Rhotic consonant|Rhotic]] | | | | |ɾ | |- ![[Lateral consonant|Lateral]] | | | |(l̠ʲ) |l |ɭ |- ![[Approximant consonant|Approximant]] | colspan="2" |w | |j | |ɻ |} */t̪/ can be heard as fricatives [θ] in intervocalic positions, and as [ð] when in between a nasal and a vowel. */ɾ/ can be heard as a trill [r] when in word-final position. */ɭ/ can be heard as an alveolo-palatal [l̠ʲ] when before /t̠ʲ/. === Vowels === {| class="wikitable IPA" style="text-align: center;" ! ![[Front vowel|Front]] ![[Back vowel|Back]] |- ![[Close vowel|Close]] |i, iː |u, uː |- ![[Open vowel|Open]] | colspan="2" |a, aː |} * /i/ can be heard as [ɪ] when before /j/ or any other alveolo-palatal laminal sounds. * /u/ can also be heard as [ʊ], and as [o] when in word-final positions.{{Cite book |last=Breen |first=Gavan |title=The Mayi languages of the Queensland Gulf Country |publisher=Canberra: AIAS |year=1981 |pages=21–31}} == References == {{reflist}} {{Pama–Nyungan languages|North}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Mayabic languages]] [[Category:Extinct languages of Queensland]] {{ia-lang-stub}}
